description: Barley Roti is an Ayurvedic flatbread made with barley flour, cooked on a medium-hot tawa — a classical recipe from Bhojana Kutuhala. Barley (Yava) balances Kapha and Pitta and is prized in Ayurveda for its lightness.

steps.text: Combine barley flour and rock salt. Gradually add warm water; knead into a soft, smooth dough. Cover and rest 15–20 min.
Divide into equal balls. Dust with flour and roll into thin, round rotis.
Cook on a medium-hot tawa. Apply ghee; cook until bubbles form, then flip. Apply ghee on second side; press gently with spatula until puffed and cooked through.
Serve hot with curry, dal, or chutney.

description: Blackgram Stuffed Paratha (Vedanika) is an Ayurvedic stuffed flatbread made with wheat flour, de-husked black gram and sesame oil, dust and roll thin — a classical recipe from Bhojana Kutuhala. Black gram (Masha) builds strength and nourishes the tissues.

steps.text: Soak de-husked black gram 6–8 hr or overnight; grind to a smooth paste.
Make soft wheat dough with rock salt and water; cover and rest 15–20 min.
Portion the paste into balls for stuffing. Flatten each dough ball, place paste in centre, seal edges.
Dust and roll thin. Cook on a medium tawa with ghee or sesame oil until golden brown spots appear on both sides. Serve hot with ghee.

prepAheadNote: Soak de-husked black gram 6–8 hr or overnight.

description: Blackgram Stuffed Puri (Vadori) is an Ayurvedic flatbread made with wheat flour and black gram, heated ghee in a deep pan — a classical recipe from Bhojana Kutuhala. Black gram (Masha) builds strength and nourishes the tissues.

steps.text: Soak black gram 6–8 hr; grind to a smooth paste.
Knead wheat flour with water into a soft dough.
Make stuffing balls from paste. Flatten dough, fill, seal, and apply a little oil; roll thin and round.
Heat ghee in a deep pan. Slide each puri in gently; press lightly with a slotted spoon to puff. Fry until both sides are golden brown. Drain on paper and serve hot.

description: Black Gram Roti is an Ayurvedic flatbread made with black gram flour, roll into thin, round rotis — a classical recipe from Bhojana Kutuhala. Black gram (Masha) builds strength and nourishes the tissues.

steps.text: Mix flour and rock salt; gradually add water and knead into a soft dough. Cover and rest 15–20 min.
Roll into thin, round rotis. Cook on a medium tawa with ghee, flipping when bubbles appear. Press gently to puff.
Serve hot with curry, dal, or chutney.

description: Wheat Roti is an Ayurvedic flatbread made with wheat flour and milk, roll into thin, round rotis — a classical recipe from Bhojana Kutuhala. Cow's milk (Dugdha) builds Ojas — the body's vital essence.

steps.text: Add milk gradually to flour; knead into a soft dough. Cover and rest 5–10 min.
Roll into thin, round rotis. Cook on a medium tawa with ghee on both sides, pressing to puff.
Serve hot with curry, dal, or chutney.

description: Baati (Angarakarakati) is an Ayurvedic flatbread made with wheat flour, divide into medium balls — a classical recipe from Bhavaprakasha. Ghee (Ghrita) kindles digestion and carries nutrients deep into the body.

steps.text: Mix flour, rock salt, and 3–4 tsp ghee. Add water gradually and knead into a firm dough. Rest 15–20 min.
Divide into medium balls. Cook using one of the following methods:
Cool slightly. Dip in melted ghee or pour ghee generously over each. Serve with dal.

description: Classical Soft Bread (Samita Roti / Mandaka) is an Ayurvedic flatbread made with refined wheat flour (samita), roll into thin, round rotis — a classical recipe from Bhojana Kutuhala.

steps.text: Add water gradually; knead into a soft, smooth dough. Cover and rest 5–10 min.
Roll into thin, round rotis. Cook on a medium tawa with ghee on both sides, pressing to puff.
Serve with milk, ghee, and rock sugar.

description: Barley Savory Discs (Kulmasha) is an Ayurvedic fritter made with barley flour, hot water and mustard oil, shape into small round discs (2–3 inches) — a classical recipe from Kaiyadeva Nighantu. Barley (Yava) balances Kapha and Pitta and is prized in Ayurveda for its lightness.

steps.text: Combine flour, rock salt, and mustard oil. Add hot water gradually; knead into a smooth dough.
Shape into small round discs (2–3 inches). Steam until fully cooked. Remove from heat and serve.

description: Vada (Vataka) is an Ayurvedic fritter made with de-husked black gram, wet ginger paste and hingu (asafoetida), heated oil over medium flame — a classical recipe from Bhojana Kutuhala. Black gram (Masha) builds strength and nourishes the tissues.

steps.text: Wash black gram; soak 4–6 hr. Drain and grind with minimal water into a smooth, thick batter. Beat until light and fluffy.
Mix in rock salt, ginger paste, and hingu.
Heat oil over medium flame. Wet hands; take batter, shape into vada with a hole in the centre. Slide gently into hot oil; deep fry until golden and crisp on both sides.
Drain on paper. Serve with a side dish of your choice.

description: Pumpkin Crunch Bites (Kushmanda Vataka) is an Ayurvedic fritter made with black gram flour, pumpkin paste and wet ginger paste, heated oil over medium flame — a classical recipe from Bhojana Kutuhala. Black gram (Masha) builds strength and nourishes the tissues.

steps.text: Combine flour, pumpkin paste, rock salt, ginger paste, hingu, black pepper, fenugreek, and cumin. Add water gradually to form a smooth, thick, fluffy batter.
Heat oil over medium flame. Shape into vada with a hole; deep fry until golden and crisp. Drain and serve.

description: Puri (Purika) is an Ayurvedic flatbread made with refined wheat flour, gram flour (besan) and cumin seeds, deep-fried in hot ghee until puffed and golden on both… — a classical recipe from Bhojana Kutuhala.

steps.text: Mix both flours with cumin, hingu, and black pepper. Add 2–3 tsp ghee and rub in. Add water gradually; knead into a soft, smooth dough.
Divide; roll each ball thin and round (applying a little ghee/oil to prevent sticking).
Deep fry in hot ghee until puffed and golden on both sides. Drain and serve hot.

description: Masala Puri (Candarika / Ghrtapura) is an Ayurvedic flatbread made with rice flour, green gram flour and black gram flour, deep-fried in hot ghee until puffed and golden on both… — a classical recipe from Bhojana Kutuhala. Black gram (Masha) builds strength and nourishes the tissues.

steps.text: Mix all three flours with cumin, hingu, and black pepper. Add 2–3 tsp ghee; mix. Add water gradually; knead into a soft, smooth dough.
Divide; roll thin and round (apply a little oil to prevent sticking).
Deep fry in hot ghee until puffed and golden on both sides. Drain and serve.

description: Karpura Crispy Sticks (Karpuranalika) is an Ayurvedic fritter made with wheat flour / samita, clove powder and edible camphor (karpura), deep-fried in ghee until golden and crispy — a classical recipe from Bhavaprakasha. Ghee (Ghrita) kindles digestion and carries nutrients deep into the body.

steps.text: Knead flour with water and ghee into a smooth dough.
Shape dough into small elongated tubes (3–5 cm).
Mix clove powder, pepper, camphor, and rock sugar into a filling powder. Stuff tubes; press and seal both ends.
Deep fry in ghee until golden and crispy.

description: Stuffed Cottage Cheese Dumplings (Dugdha Kupika) is an Ayurvedic sweet ball made with cow's milk, lemon juice and rice flour, **Make chena:** Boil milk — a classical recipe from Bhavaprakasha. Cow's milk (Dugdha) builds Ojas — the body's vital essence.

steps.text: **Make chena:** Boil milk; add lemon juice gradually while stirring until milk curdles. Strain through muslin, wash with clean water, hang 20–30 min to drain.
**Dough:** Add rice flour to chena; knead 8–10 min until smooth and crack-free.
**Shape:** Divide into 3–4 balls (25–30 g each). Roll smooth.
**First fry:** Deep fry in medium-hot ghee until light golden. Cool slightly.
**Stuff:** Make a small cavity in each; fill with reserved chena mixed with a little sugar and camphor. Seal.
**Second fry:** Fry again until golden brown. Drain.
**Syrup:** Boil 20 g sugar in 40 ml water to 1–2 thread consistency; add a pinch of camphor.
**Soak:** Immerse dumplings in warm syrup for 10–15 min. Serve warm.

description: Pumpkin & Big Beans Sweet Pancake is an Ayurvedic flatbread made with ripe pumpkin, chopped, cowpeas / soybeans and ragi flour, add ragi paste to the cooked pumpkin — a classical recipe from AYUSH. Jaggery and rock sugar are considered cleaner sweeteners than refined sugar in Ayurveda.

steps.text: Soak cowpeas/soybeans 4 hr; pressure cook until soft. Add pumpkin pieces; cook further with a glass of water.
Mix ragi flour into 1 cup water to a smooth paste (no lumps).
Add ragi paste to the cooked pumpkin; boil, stirring. Add jaggery syrup, coconut, and ghee; mix well.
Heat a lightly greased pan; pour a ladle of batter, spread gently. Cook until edges set; flip and cook until golden brown.

sources.text: Traditional food recipes from Ayush systems of medicine

description: Green Gram & Fenugreek Chila is an Ayurvedic flatbread made with green gram sprouts, chopped fenugreek leaves and ginger, heated a flat pan — a classical recipe from AYUSH.

steps.text: Grind sprouts with ginger to a smooth batter consistency.
Add fenugreek leaves, Bengal gram flour, turmeric, and salt; mix well. Rest 15 min.
Heat a flat pan; grease lightly with oil. Pour a ladleful of batter; spread in a circular motion. Cook until crispy. Serve with a side dish.

sources.text: Traditional food recipes from Ayush systems of medicine

description: Fresh Fenugreek Stir Fry (Methika) is an Ayurvedic preparation made with methi (fenugreek) leaves and hingu, boiled in water 3–5 min until soft — a classical recipe from Ksemakutūhalam. Ghee (Ghrita) kindles digestion and carries nutrients deep into the body.

steps.text: Clean methi leaves thoroughly with water.
Boil in water 3–5 min until soft; squeeze out excess water to form a compact mass.
Heat ghee; add hingu, then the squeezed methi mass and rock salt. Roast properly.

description: Punjabi Greens is an Ayurvedic preparation made with dark green leafy vegetable, ghee / oil and cumin seeds, heated oil — a classical recipe from Morningstar.

steps.text: Wash and chop greens.
Heat oil; add cumin, turmeric, and hingu.
Add garlic paste and onion (optional); fry until golden brown.
Add greens; cook on medium heat until done. Season with rock salt as needed.

sources.text: Morningstar — Ayurvedic Cooking for All, 3rd repr. 2011

description: Brinjal Fry is an Ayurvedic preparation made with brinjal, lemon juice and hingu, heated oil — a classical recipe from Ksemakutūhalam.

steps.text: Wash and slice brinjal thin.
Heat oil; fry brinjal on medium flame, stirring occasionally, until soft and edges are crispy.
Add hingu, ginger paste, and rock salt; cook 2–3 min more. Turn off flame.
Add lemon juice; mix well. Cover 3–5 min. Garnish with coriander leaves before serving.

description: Parval Fry (Patola) is an Ayurvedic preparation made with pointed gourd (parval) and hingu, heated ghee — a classical recipe from Ksemakutūhalam. Ghee (Ghrita) kindles digestion and carries nutrients deep into the body.

steps.text: Wash and slice pointed gourd thin.
Heat ghee; fry slices on medium flame, stirring occasionally.
Add hingu, rock salt, and any additional spices to taste. Cook dry on moderate flame until soft.
Turn off flame; cover 3–5 min. Serve hot.

description: Smoky Eggplant Delight is an Ayurvedic preparation made with eggplant, mustard seeds and cumin seeds, heated oil — a classical recipe from Gowans.

steps.text: Slice eggplant; sprinkle with salt, let sweat, wash off salt, and pat dry.
Heat oil; pop mustard seeds, then cumin, curry leaves, and onion. Stir.
When onion is translucent, add turmeric. Add eggplant; cover and cook until soft. Season with salt.

sources.text: Gowans — Food for Life: Ayurvedic Recipes, 2009

description: Smoky Golden Delight is an Ayurvedic preparation made with sliced pumpkin, sliced almonds and mustard seeds, steamed pumpkin cubes until soft — a classical recipe from Gowans. Ghee (Ghrita) kindles digestion and carries nutrients deep into the body.

steps.text: Steam pumpkin cubes until soft.
Heat ghee; pop mustard seeds, then cumin, curry leaves, and onion until golden.
In a separate pan, toast sliced almonds until golden.
Add steamed pumpkin to the spice pan; fry. Add almonds, turmeric, and salt. Mix well; cover 3–4 min.

sources.text: Gowans — Food for Life: Ayurvedic Recipes, 2009

description: Sweet Aloo Sauté is an Ayurvedic preparation made with chopped pumpkin, chopped sweet potato and mustard seeds, steamed pumpkin and sweet potato until soft — a classical recipe from Gowans. Ghee (Ghrita) kindles digestion and carries nutrients deep into the body.

steps.text: Steam pumpkin and sweet potato until soft.
Heat ghee; add mustard seeds, cumin, curry leaves, onion, ginger paste, and turmeric. Fry well.
Add steamed vegetables; season with rock salt. Mix; cover 2–3 min.

sources.text: Gowans — Food for Life: Ayurvedic Recipes, 2009

description: Gooseberry Stir Fry is an Ayurvedic preparation made with indian gooseberry (amla), sesame oil and curry leaves, heated sesame oil — a classical recipe from AYUSH. Amla (Amalaki) is the supreme rasayana, balancing all three doshas.

steps.text: Wash and dry amla; cut and remove seeds.
Heat sesame oil; fry amla pieces well.
Add curry leaves, pepper, turmeric, salt, and hingu; mix well. Serve as a side dish.

sources.text: Traditional food recipes from Ayush systems of medicine

description: Ginger Barfi (Ardraka Paka) is an Ayurvedic halwa made with fresh ginger, jaggery and dry ginger powder, cooked jaggery until a thick syrup forms — a classical recipe from AYUSH. Jaggery and rock sugar are considered cleaner sweeteners than refined sugar in Ayurveda.

steps.text: Cook jaggery until a thick syrup forms. Add grated ginger; stir and cook 5–7 min on low flame.
Add ghee; mix well and cook 5–10 min more. Add powdered spices; cook another 5–10 min.
Add sesame seeds if desired. Pour onto a ghee-greased plate; spread evenly.
Cool before cutting into pieces. Store in an airtight container.

sources.text: Traditional food recipes from Ayush systems of medicine

description: Coconut Laddu (Narikela Modaka) is an Ayurvedic sweet ball made with grated coconut, milk and rock sugar powder, cooked grated coconut in milk until well cooked — a classical recipe from Ksemakutūhalam. Coconut cools, rejuvenates and nourishes all seven tissues.

steps.text: Cook grated coconut in milk until well cooked.
Roast the cooked coconut in ghee until properly done.
Prepare a sugar syrup in a separate pan with rock sugar and water; boil to a proper binding consistency.
Add roasted coconut to the syrup. Add cardamom and dry ginger powder; mix well.
Shape into small laddoos while warm.

description: Sweet Coconut Momo (Bhaimi) is an Ayurvedic sweet ball made with wheat flour, grated coconut and dry grapes, **Filling:** Heat ghee — a classical recipe from Ksemakutūhalam. Ghee (Ghrita) kindles digestion and carries nutrients deep into the body.

steps.text: **Dough:** Mix wheat flour with ghee and water; knead into soft dough.
**Filling:** Heat ghee; add coconut, dry grapes, dates, rock sugar, and aromatic powder. Roast on medium flame; work into a paste.
**Shape:** Divide dough into small balls; roll thin. Place filling in centre; fold and pleat edges to seal.
Deep fry in ghee on low–medium flame until golden brown.

description: Urad Amrut Laddu (Masha Ladduka) is an Ayurvedic sweet ball made with de-husked black gram, rock sugar powder and aromatic powder, **Boondi:** Heat ghee — a classical recipe from Ksemakutūhalam. Black gram (Masha) builds strength and nourishes the tissues.

steps.text: **Batter:** Soak black gram 4–6 hr; grind with minimal water to a soft, pouring batter.
**Boondi:** Heat ghee; hold a perforated ladle over ghee, pour batter through, tapping to make small drops. Fry until cooked but not crispy. Drain.
**Syrup:** Dissolve sugar in water; heat to syrup consistency. Add aromatic powder.
**Assembly:** Add fried boondi to hot syrup; mix so boondi absorbs syrup. Add ghee-roasted dry fruits. Shape into laddoos while warm; add a little warm syrup/water if mixture is too dry.

description: Wheat Balls (Godhuma Laddu) is an Ayurvedic sweet ball made with wheat flour, jaggery and cardamom powder, heated ghee — a classical recipe from ICMR-NIN. Ghee (Ghrita) kindles digestion and carries nutrients deep into the body.

steps.text: Heat ghee; add wheat flour and roast on medium flame until done.
In a separate pan, make jaggery syrup with enough water to a binding consistency.
Turn off flame; slowly fold in roasted flour, stirring continuously to avoid lumps. Add cardamom and dry ginger; mix.
Shape into laddoos while still warm. Add a little ghee or warm syrup if mixture is too dry.

Calorie-dense preparation — portion carefully.
Rich in fat or sugar — balance with physical activity.

description: Jamun (Manda) is an Ayurvedic preserve made with refined wheat flour, rock sugar and aromatic powder, fried balls in medium-hot ghee until golden brown on a… — a classical recipe from Bhojana Kutuhala. Ghee (Ghrita) kindles digestion and carries nutrients deep into the body.

steps.text: Mix flour with 2–3 tsp melted ghee; add water gradually and knead into a soft, smooth dough.
Divide; roll into smooth, crack-free balls.
Fry balls in medium-hot ghee until golden brown on all sides. Drain.
Prepare sugar syrup with aromatic powder. Turn off flame.
Once balls cool to moderate temperature, transfer to warm syrup. Soak 2–3 hr. Enjoy.

Rich in fat or sugar — balance with physical activity.

description: Golden Bliss Laddu (Samita Modak) is an Ayurvedic sweet ball made with refined wheat flour, rock sugar powder and aromatic powder, form into medium balls — a classical recipe from Bhojana Kutuhala. Ghee (Ghrita) kindles digestion and carries nutrients deep into the body.

steps.text: Make a firm dough with flour, a pinch of rock salt, ghee, and water. Rest 15–20 min.
Form into medium balls. Cook using any baati method (see S-06) — charcoal, oven (180 °C / 25–30 min), air fryer, pressure cooker, or stovetop. Cool completely.
Powder the cooked balls in a mixing bowl. Add rock sugar powder and aromatic powder; mix. Add ghee as needed to bind into laddoos.

description: Date Laddoo (Kharjur Laddoo) is an Ayurvedic sweet ball made with dates (kharjur), cashews and almonds, lightly roast nuts in 2 tsp ghee until golden — a classical recipe from AYUSH. Coconut cools, rejuvenates and nourishes all seven tissues.

steps.text: Remove seeds from dates; chop small. Chop cashews and almonds.
Lightly roast nuts in 2 tsp ghee until golden. Mix in chopped dates.
Shape mixture into small laddoos; roll in grated coconut. (Roasted sesame seeds may be used instead.)

sources.text: Traditional food recipes from Ayush systems of medicine

description: Sweet Vermicelli Balls (Sevika Modaka) is an Ayurvedic sweet ball made with fine wheat flour (samita) and rock sugar, heated ghee — a classical recipe from Bhavaprakasha. Ghee (Ghrita) kindles digestion and carries nutrients deep into the body.

steps.text: Knead flour with ghee and enough water into a smooth dough.
Heat ghee; hold a perforated ladle over ghee, pour batter through to make small drops. Fry until crispy and golden.
Immerse fried pieces in one-thread sugar syrup until absorbed.
Remove from syrup; shape into small balls (modaka).

Calorie-dense preparation — portion carefully.
Rich in fat or sugar — balance with physical activity.

description: Milky Wheat Balls (Dravaka Modaka) is an Ayurvedic sweet ball made with fine wheat flour (samita), rock sugar and cow's milk (dugdha), cooked on low heat — a classical recipe from Bhojana Kutuhala. Jaggery and rock sugar are considered cleaner sweeteners than refined sugar in Ayurveda.

steps.text: Combine flour, milk, and ghee; mix into a thin batter.
Cook on low heat; once half cooked, add ghee and continue until thicker.
Remove from heat; cool. Add equal amount of sugar; mix thoroughly. Shape into small balls.

healthFlags.note: High in sugars or glycaemic load — consume sparingly.

description: Processed Wheat Balls (Samita Modaka) is an Ayurvedic sweet ball made with fine wheat flour (samita), rock sugar and clove, fried Samita in ghee until colour changes — a classical recipe from Bhojana Kutuhala. Ghee (Ghrita) kindles digestion and carries nutrients deep into the body.

steps.text: Fry Samita in ghee until colour changes; cool.
Add rock sugar and powdered cardamom, clove, and pepper; mix thoroughly.
Shape into small balls.

healthFlags.note: High in sugars or glycaemic load — consume sparingly.
Calorie-dense preparation — portion carefully.
Rich in fat or sugar — balance with physical activity.

description: Camphor Vermicelli Balls (Chitta Modaka) is an Ayurvedic sweet ball made with wheat flour, rock sugar and edible camphor (karpura), heated ghee — a classical recipe from Ksemakutūhalam. Ghee (Ghrita) kindles digestion and carries nutrients deep into the body.

steps.text: Knead flour with ghee and water into a smooth dough.
Heat ghee; pass batter through a perforated ladle to form drops. Fry until crispy and golden.
Immerse in one-thread sugar syrup until absorbed.
Remove; add edible camphor and shape into small balls.

Rich in fat or sugar — balance with physical activity.

description: Gooseberry Fruit Preserve (Amalaki Murabba) is an Ayurvedic preserve made with fresh amla, sugar and food-grade lime water, make syrup: dissolve 200 g sugar in 100 ml water — a classical recipe from Ayurveda. Amla (Amalaki) is the supreme rasayana, balancing all three doshas.

steps.text: Dissolve food-grade lime (calcium hydroxide) in water; let particles settle; use only the clear supernatant.
Wash amla; prick each 8–10 times with a clean fork. Submerge completely in lime water. Cover and keep at room temperature 3–4 days, replacing lime water every 24 hr.
Wash amla thoroughly 2–3 times to remove residual lime.
Make syrup: dissolve 200 g sugar in 100 ml water; boil to syrup consistency. Add washed amla; simmer on low heat 10–15 min until well coated without breaking.
Cool; transfer amla and syrup to a sterilized glass jar. Rest 2–3 days for full absorption. Serve 1–2 fruits with a little syrup per serving.

sources.citation: Ayurveda sara Samgraha — Avaleha-Paka Prakarana, p. 532

description: Milky Coconut Delight (Narikela Ksheerika) is an Ayurvedic sweet milk preparation made with cow's milk and fresh grated coconut, cooked grated coconut in milk until a thick consistenc… — a classical recipe from Ksemakutūhalam. Cow's milk (Dugdha) builds Ojas — the body's vital essence.

steps.text: Cook grated coconut in milk until a thick consistency is reached.
Spread evenly on a flat plate; cool slightly. Cut into small pieces and serve.

Rich in fat or sugar — balance with physical activity.

description: Sweet Potato Salad is an Ayurvedic preparation made with sweet potato, fresh ginger paste and fresh lemon juice, boiled sweet potato — a classical recipe from Morningstar.

steps.text: Boil sweet potato; peel and cut into medium square cubes.
In a mixing bowl, combine sweet potato with ginger paste, lemon juice, honey, and rock salt.
Heat sesame oil and drizzle over. Toss well. Serve warm or cool.

sources.text: Morningstar — Ayurvedic Cooking for All, 3rd repr. 2011

description: Sweet Potato Biscuits is an Ayurvedic fritter made with wheat flour / barley flour, baking powder and baking soda, add sweet potato, lemon juice, and milk — a classical recipe from Morningstar. Barley (Yava) balances Kapha and Pitta and is prized in Ayurveda for its lightness.

steps.text: Mix flour, salt, baking powder, and baking soda. Add butter/ghee; mix well.
Add sweet potato, lemon juice, and milk; mix into a soft dough (adjust flour or milk as needed). Rest 15 min. Preheat oven to 450 °F.
Roll gently; cut into biscuit shapes. Place on a greased baking tray.
Bake until light golden brown. Cool completely. Store in an airtight container.

sources.text: Morningstar — Ayurvedic Cooking for All, 3rd repr. 2011

description: Banana Apricot Muffins is an Ayurvedic preparation made with dried organic apricot, ripe banana and almond oil, pour into a lightly oiled muffin tin — a classical recipe from Morningstar. Barley (Yava) balances Kapha and Pitta and is prized in Ayurveda for its lightness.

steps.text: Soak apricots in hot water 15 min; finely chop.
Mash bananas; combine with almond oil and maple syrup.
Add flour, baking powder, and salt; fold in chopped apricot. Add water to reach a thick batter.
Pour into a lightly oiled muffin tin. Bake at 350 °F for ~25 min until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool before serving.

sources.text: Morningstar — Ayurvedic Cooking for All, 3rd repr. 2011

description: Almond Nut Crust is an Ayurvedic preparation made with finely ground raw almonds, brown sugar (powdered) and wheat flour / barley flour, baked ~15 min or until light golden — a classical recipe from Morningstar. Barley (Yava) balances Kapha and Pitta and is prized in Ayurveda for its lightness.

steps.text: Mix flour, almond powder, powdered sugar, and salt. Add cold butter and cold water; make a dough.
Rest 15 min. Preheat oven to 375 °F.
Roll gently; cut into shapes. Place on a greased baking tray.
Bake ~15 min or until light golden. Cool completely. Store in an airtight container.

sources.text: Morningstar — Ayurvedic Cooking for All, 3rd repr. 2011

description: Coconut Sesame Rice is an Ayurvedic rice preparation made with rice, sesame seeds and desiccated coconut, cooked rice with water, ghee, and rock salt — a classical recipe from Morningstar. Ghee (Ghrita) kindles digestion and carries nutrients deep into the body.

steps.text: Cook rice with water, ghee, and rock salt.
Heat ghee; toast sesame seeds and desiccated coconut until slightly darkened.
Add cooked rice; mix well. Garnish with coriander leaves.

sources.text: Morningstar — Ayurvedic Cooking for All, 3rd repr. 2011

description: Steamed Rice Cake (Indarika Idli) is an Ayurvedic rice preparation made with rice flour and black gram flour, steamed in an idli maker or steamer until properly cooked — a classical recipe from Ayurveda. Black gram (Masha) builds strength and nourishes the tissues.

steps.text: Mix both flours with water to a smooth batter — not too thick or thin. Ferment overnight.
Next morning, add rock salt to the fermented batter; mix well.
Steam in an idli maker or steamer until properly cooked.

description: Coconut Water Drink (Hemakirana Panaka) is an Ayurvedic cooling drink made with coconut water, rock sugar powder and citron fruit juice (rough lemon) — a classical recipe from Ksemakutūhalam. Jaggery and rock sugar are considered cleaner sweeteners than refined sugar in Ayurveda.

steps.text: Combine coconut water and rock sugar; stir to dissolve.
Add lemon juice; mix.
Filter through a sieve and serve.

description: Fresh Mango Fusion (Prapanaka) is an Ayurvedic cooling drink made with raw mango, rock sugar and aromatic powder, boiled raw mango in a pressure cooker or pot until soft — a classical recipe from Bhojana Kutuhala. Jaggery and rock sugar are considered cleaner sweeteners than refined sugar in Ayurveda.

steps.text: Boil raw mango in a pressure cooker or pot until soft. Cool; remove skin and squeeze to a smooth liquid paste.
Add rock sugar, cold water (not refrigerated), aromatic powder, and rock salt; stir. Serve immediately.

description: Golden Essence (Dhanyaka Panaka) is an Ayurvedic cooling drink made with coriander seeds, sugar and edible camphor — a classical recipe from Bhojana Kutuhala.

steps.text: Wash coriander seeds; soak 20–30 min. Macerate thoroughly with mortar and pestle or grinding slab.
Filter through a cloth with sufficient water. Add rock sugar powder and fine camphor; mix well.

description: Citrus Spark (Amalaki Panaka) is an Ayurvedic cooling drink made with fresh amla, dry ginger powder and cardamom powder, steamed amla until soft — a classical recipe from AYUSH. Amla (Amalaki) is the supreme rasayana, balancing all three doshas.

steps.text: Steam amla until soft; cool, remove seeds, grind to smooth paste.
Add 1 glass water to paste; mix. Add dry ginger, cardamom, rock sugar/jaggery, rock salt, and honey; stir well. Serve fresh.

sources.text: Traditional food recipes from Ayush systems of medicine

description: Sweet Elixir (Sharkarodak) is an Ayurvedic cooling drink made with cold water, rock sugar and aromatic powder — a classical recipe from Bhojana Kutuhala. Jaggery and rock sugar are considered cleaner sweeteners than refined sugar in Ayurveda.

steps.text: Dissolve rock sugar in cold water (not refrigerated).
Add aromatic powder and rock salt; stir well.
Serve as needed.

description: Sunshine Sip (Kharjuradi Mantha) is an Ayurvedic cooling drink made with seedless grapes, soft dates and roasted puffed paddy — a classical recipe from AYUSH. Jaggery and rock sugar are considered cleaner sweeteners than refined sugar in Ayurveda.

steps.text: Soak grapes and dates in water 1 hr.
Blend with soaked fruit, water, puffed paddy, and jaggery until smooth.
Serve fresh.

sources.text: Traditional food recipes from Ayush systems of medicine

prepAheadNote: Soak grapes and dates in water 1 hr.

description: Amla Squash is an Ayurvedic cooling drink made with amla, candy sugar and roasted cumin powder, boiled amla until soft — a classical recipe from AYUSH. Amla (Amalaki) is the supreme rasayana, balancing all three doshas.

steps.text: Boil amla until soft; cool, remove seeds, grind to smooth paste.
Make a one-strand sugar syrup (double the paste quantity) in a separate pan.
Combine pulp and syrup; mix. Add water if needed. Add rock salt, cumin powder, pepper, and black salt; stir well. Serve fresh.

sources.text: Traditional food recipes from Ayush systems of medicine

description: Masala Curd (Rasala) is an Ayurvedic spiced buttermilk drink made with fresh curd, pepper powder and jaggery / sugar, heated ghee — a classical recipe from AYUSH. Jaggery and rock sugar are considered cleaner sweeteners than refined sugar in Ayurveda.

steps.text: Add pepper, jaggery/sugar, and salt to curd; blend or churn until smooth.
Heat ghee; splutter mustard seeds, add fenugreek, cumin, red chilli, and curry leaves. Use as seasoning over curd mixture.
Serve with roti or rice.

sources.text: Traditional food recipes from Ayush systems of medicine

description: Masala Buttermilk (Rasala) is an Ayurvedic spiced buttermilk drink made with fresh curd, pepper powder and jaggery / sugar, heated ghee — a classical recipe from AYUSH. Jaggery and rock sugar are considered cleaner sweeteners than refined sugar in Ayurveda.

steps.text: Blend curd, water, pepper, jaggery/sugar, and salt until smooth buttermilk consistency.
Heat ghee; splutter mustard, add fenugreek, cumin, red chilli, and curry leaves. Add seasoning to buttermilk; add lemon juice; mix well. Serve fresh.

sources.text: Traditional food recipes from Ayush systems of medicine

description: Tempered Buttermilk (Khalam) is an Ayurvedic spiced buttermilk drink made with buttermilk, fresh ginger paste and hingu, heated buttermilk on medium flame — a classical recipe from AYUSH.

steps.text: Heat buttermilk on medium flame; add ginger paste and boil 1 min.
Add turmeric, pepper, hingu, and rock salt; mix well.
Turn off flame.
Serve hot.

sources.text: Traditional food recipes from Ayush systems of medicine

description: Green Gram Soup is an Ayurvedic medicinal soup made with green gram, pepper and mustard seeds, heated ghee — a classical recipe from Ksemakutūhalam. Ghee (Ghrita) kindles digestion and carries nutrients deep into the body.

steps.text: Soak green gram 4–5 hr. Pressure cook with water until soft.
Mash lightly or partially blend to a smooth soup consistency.
Heat ghee; splutter mustard, add fenugreek and curry leaves; pour into soup.
Add rock salt, pepper, and lemon juice; mix. Serve.

description: Blackgram Soup is an Ayurvedic medicinal soup made with black gram, pepper and mustard seeds, heated ghee — a classical recipe from Ksemakutūhalam. Black gram (Masha) builds strength and nourishes the tissues.

steps.text: Soak black gram 4–5 hr. Cook until soft and well done.
Mash lightly or partially blend to a smooth soup consistency.
Heat ghee; splutter mustard, add fenugreek and curry leaves; pour into soup.
Add rock salt, pepper, and lemon juice; mix. Serve.

description: Green Soup is an Ayurvedic medicinal soup made with fenugreek / spinach / any green leafy vegetable, finely chopped onion and finely chopped ripe tomato, heated oil — a classical recipe from AYUSH.

ingredients.nameEn: Fenugreek / spinach / any green leafy vegetable

steps.text: Heat oil; fry onion and garlic paste. Add tomato; cook 2–3 min. Add greens; cook until soft.
Add dal water and salt; simmer 15 min.
Take half the soup, cool, and blend smooth; return to pot. Simmer 5 min more.
Add pepper; mix. Serve.

sources.text: Traditional food recipes from Ayush systems of medicine

description: Sweet Potato Soup is an Ayurvedic medicinal soup made with sweet potato, fresh ginger and cow's milk, boiled sweet potato with ginger until soft — a classical recipe from Morningstar. Cow's milk (Dugdha) builds Ojas — the body's vital essence.

steps.text: Boil sweet potato with ginger until soft.
Blend boiled sweet potato (peeled), ginger, hot milk, salt, optional sugar, spices, and pepper until smooth.
Add more milk or water to reach a creamy consistency. Serve fresh and hot.

sources.text: Morningstar — Ayurvedic Cooking for All, 3rd repr. 2011

description: Beet Borscht is an Ayurvedic medicinal soup made with sliced beetroot, fresh ginger and olive oil, boiled in water until beetroot is soft — a classical recipe from Morningstar.

steps.text: Peel and slice beetroot and ginger.
Boil in water until beetroot is soft.
Blend boiled beetroot and ginger with water, olive oil, salt, and black pepper until smooth.
Add more water for desired consistency. Serve fresh.

sources.text: Morningstar — Ayurvedic Cooking for All, 3rd repr. 2011

description: Split Moong Soup is an Ayurvedic medicinal soup made with split mung dal, hingu and fresh ginger, boiled mung dal with water, chopped ginger, and hingu … — a classical recipe from Morningstar.

steps.text: Boil mung dal with water, chopped ginger, and hingu until soft and fully cooked.
Blend with ginger, coriander, cumin, salt, and olive oil until smooth.
Add water to reach creamy consistency. Serve fresh and hot.

sources.text: Morningstar — Ayurvedic Cooking for All, 3rd repr. 2011

description: Coconut Payasa (Nalikera Ksirika) is an Ayurvedic sweet milk preparation made with grated tender coconut, milk and rock sugar, fried grated coconut in ghee until slightly golden — a classical recipe from Ksemakutūhalam. Coconut cools, rejuvenates and nourishes all seven tissues.

steps.text: Fry grated coconut in ghee until slightly golden. Add boiled milk; stir continuously until thickened.
Add sugar; stir until dissolved. Add aromatic powder and ghee-roasted dry fruits; mix well.

description: Milk Delight (Pindaka) is an Ayurvedic sweet milk preparation made with cow's milk, rock sugar powder and aromatic powder, gently boil milk — a classical recipe from Ksemakutūhalam. Cow's milk (Dugdha) builds Ojas — the body's vital essence.

steps.text: Gently boil milk; add rock sugar and stir until dissolved.
Boil until mildly thick. Add aromatic powder; cook 2–3 min more. Serve hot or warm.

description: Revitalizing Milk (Mashadi Ksheerapaka) is an Ayurvedic sweet milk preparation made with black gram powder, milk and rock sugar powder, heated ghee — a classical recipe from Bhaishajya Ratnavali. Black gram (Masha) builds strength and nourishes the tissues.

steps.text: Heat ghee; roast black gram powder until golden.
Add milk; bring to a gentle boil.
Add rock sugar; stir until dissolved.
Boil 2–3 min.
Serve hot or warm.

description: Ginger Milk is an Ayurvedic sweet milk preparation made with milk, fresh ginger paste and honey (optional), combined milk and water — a classical recipe from Morningstar. Cow's milk (Dugdha) builds Ojas — the body's vital essence.

steps.text: Combine milk and water; bring to heat. Add ginger paste; boil 3–5 min until reduced to ~1 cup.
Strain and serve with honey to taste.

sources.text: Morningstar — Ayurvedic Cooking for All, 3rd repr. 2011

shelfLife: Same day; up to 1 day refrigerated

description: Restorative Almond Drink is an Ayurvedic cooling drink made with almonds, milk and rose petals — a classical recipe from Morningstar. Cow's milk (Dugdha) builds Ojas — the body's vital essence.

steps.text: Soak almonds overnight; remove skins.
Blend with milk, water, cardamom, saffron, rose petals, and honey until smooth. Serve.

sources.text: Morningstar — Ayurvedic Cooking for All, 3rd repr. 2011

description: Almond Milk is an Ayurvedic sweet milk preparation made with almonds — a classical recipe from Morningstar.

steps.text: Soak almonds overnight; remove skins.
Blend with water until smooth. Strain for a smoother consistency.
Serve with optional honey as sweetener.

sources.text: Morningstar — Ayurvedic Cooking for All, 3rd repr. 2011

shelfLife: Same day; up to 1 day refrigerated

description: Spiced Milk is an Ayurvedic sweet milk preparation made with milk, crushed cardamom and ginger paste, combined milk and water — a classical recipe from Gowans. Cow's milk (Dugdha) builds Ojas — the body's vital essence.

steps.text: Combine milk and water; bring to a boil.
Add crushed cardamom, ginger paste, and turmeric. Boil until reduced by half (~1 cup).
Strain cardamom pods and ginger. Serve hot.

sources.text: Gowans — Food for Life: Ayurvedic Recipes, 2009

shelfLife: Same day; up to 1 day refrigerated

description: Barley Delight (Yava Ksheera) is an Ayurvedic sweet milk preparation made with barley, cow's milk and cow's ghee, add remaining milk — a classical recipe from Charaka Chikitsasthana. Barley (Yava) balances Kapha and Pitta and is prized in Ayurveda for its lightness.

steps.text: Mix barley flour (or ground barley) with a little milk to form a smooth paste.
Add remaining milk; cook over low flame with continuous stirring until barley is fully cooked.
Add ghee, mix well, and serve warm.

shelfLife: Same day; up to 1 day refrigerated

description: Blackgram Porridge (Vrushya Yavagu) is an Ayurvedic porridge made with split black gram and milk, bring milk to a boil in a vessel — a classical recipe from CS. Black gram (Masha) builds strength and nourishes the tissues.

steps.text: Wash split black gram thoroughly.
Bring milk to a boil in a vessel; add black gram and boil on medium flame until fully soft and semi-solid consistency is reached (add more milk if needed).
Add ghee; mix well. Serve.

shelfLife: Same day; up to 1 day refrigerated

description: Shrikandha (Rasala) is an Ayurvedic strained yogurt preparation made with fresh curd, rock sugar powder and cardamom powder — a classical recipe from Ksemakutūhalam. Jaggery and rock sugar are considered cleaner sweeteners than refined sugar in Ayurveda.

steps.text: Hang fresh curd in muslin cloth 4–6 hr or overnight to drain all water.
Transfer thick hung curd to a bowl. Add sugar, cardamom, cinnamon, ginger, and saffron (soaked in a little milk first).
Mix well. Garnish with chopped almonds and pistachios if desired. Serve.

prepAheadNote: Hang fresh curd in muslin cloth 4–6 hr or overnight to drain all water.

description: Creamy Eggplant Delight is an Ayurvedic sweet milk preparation made with brinjal, mustard seeds and jeera (cumin), steamed brinjal 10–15 min until soft and well cooked — a classical recipe from Ksemakutūhalam. Ghee (Ghrita) kindles digestion and carries nutrients deep into the body.

steps.text: Steam brinjal 10–15 min until soft and well cooked; cool.
Remove stalk; mash thoroughly until smooth.
Heat ghee; splutter mustard and cumin. Add mashed brinjal; mix well. Turn off flame and cool.
Fold in yoghurt and rock salt; mix well. Cover 3–5 min before serving.

shelfLife: Same day; up to 1 day refrigerated

description: Amla Blend (Amalaka Phala) is an Ayurvedic sweet milk preparation made with indian gooseberry (amla), jeera (cumin) and saindhava (rock salt), steamed amla 10–15 min until soft — a classical recipe from Ksemakutūhalam. Amla (Amalaki) is the supreme rasayana, balancing all three doshas.

steps.text: Steam amla 10–15 min until soft; cool, remove seeds, crush well.
Heat ghee; add cumin — let crackle. Add hingu.
Add crushed amla; fry until cooked properly. Add rock salt; mix well.

shelfLife: Same day; up to 1 day refrigerated

description: Sesame Chutney is an Ayurvedic chutney made with black sesame seeds, peanut and coriander leaves, dry roast peanuts until lightly golden — a classical recipe from AYUSH. Sesame (Tila) strengthens bones, nourishes the skin and has a warming quality.

steps.text: Dry roast peanuts until lightly golden; cool. Dry roast sesame on low flame — do not burn.
Grind all ingredients (roasted peanuts, sesame, garlic, pepper, cumin, coriander, rock sugar, rock salt) with water to a smooth chutney consistency.
Add lemon juice; mix well. Serve with any dish.

sources.text: Traditional food recipes from Ayush systems of medicine

description: Green Chutney is an Ayurvedic chutney made with drumstick / fenugreek / spinach leaves, peanut / bengal gram / black gram and grated coconut, dry roast legumes and fenugreek seeds — a classical recipe from AYUSH. Black gram (Masha) builds strength and nourishes the tissues.

steps.text: Dry roast legumes and fenugreek seeds; set aside. Dry roast cumin, coriander seeds, and cloves; cool.
Grind roasted ingredients with coconut and water/curd to a smooth paste.
Add green leaves, tomato, pepper, rock salt, jaggery, and tamarind; blend until smooth.
Optional: season with oil, mustard seeds, curry leaves, and red chillies.

sources.text: Traditional food recipes from Ayush systems of medicine

description: Date & Tamarind Chutney is an Ayurvedic chutney made with tamarind paste, dates (pitted) and brown sugar, combined all ingredients in a pan — a classical recipe from Gowans.

steps.text: Combine all ingredients in a pan; cook well together, mixing thoroughly.
Serve with plain rice.

sources.text: Gowans — Food for Life: Ayurvedic Recipes, 2009

description: Golden Grain Halwa (Lalita) is an Ayurvedic halwa made with wheat flour, rock sugar powder and priyala (chironji), heated remaining ghee — a classical recipe from Ksemakutūhalam. Ghee (Ghrita) kindles digestion and carries nutrients deep into the body.

steps.text: Toast dry fruits and chironji in ghee until golden; set aside.
Heat remaining ghee; roast wheat flour on medium flame until done.
Add sugar, roasted dry fruits, and chironji. Add milk gradually, stirring continuously to prevent lumps.
Add more ghee if needed. Cook, stirring until the mixture leaves the sides of the pan and reaches a smooth halwa consistency. Add aromatic powder; mix well.

description: Ash Gourd Treat (Khanda Kusmanda) is an Ayurvedic sweet milk preparation made with chopped ash gourd, milk and rock sugar powder, steamed ash gourd 15–20 min until soft — a classical recipe from Ksemakutūhalam. Cow's milk (Dugdha) builds Ojas — the body's vital essence.

steps.text: Steam ash gourd 15–20 min until soft.
Cook steamed pieces in milk on medium flame, stirring, until milk is absorbed. Mash to a smooth consistency (add more milk as needed).
Heat ghee in a pan; sauté mashed ash gourd 8–10 min until raw smell disappears.
Add sugar; mix well and cook to a halwa consistency. Add ghee-roasted dry fruits and aromatic powder; cook 2–3 min. Serve hot or warm.

steps.text: Grind coconut without much water — keep slightly coarse.
Boil milk; add coarse coconut and cook on medium flame, stirring continuously 5–8 min until mildly thick.
Add rock sugar; stir to dissolve. Add ghee and aromatic powder (optional); mix 1 min. Switch off flame. Garnish with dry fruits. Serve hot or warm.

steps.text: Heat ghee on low flame; add wheat flour and roast well on medium flame.
Add milk and sugar; stir continuously until mixture solidifies.
Add aromatic powder; mix well. Serve.

description: Breakfast Rice is an Ayurvedic rice preparation made with cooked rice, cow's milk and dry coriander powder, heated milk on medium flame — a classical recipe from Morningstar. Cow's milk (Dugdha) builds Ojas — the body's vital essence.

steps.text: Heat milk on medium flame; bring to a boil.
Add soft cooked rice, coriander powder, cardamom powder, and ghee; simmer 5 min.
Serve as is, or blend smooth for a creamier texture. Add optional honey if desired.

sources.text: Morningstar — Ayurvedic Cooking for All, 3rd repr. 2011

description: Rice Almond Breakfast Cereal is an Ayurvedic rice preparation made with uncooked rice, raw almonds and rock sugar, boiled 3 cups water with a pinch of rock salt — a classical recipe from Morningstar. Ghee (Ghrita) kindles digestion and carries nutrients deep into the body.

steps.text: Soak almonds overnight; grind to a fine powder or paste.
Grind rice to a fine powder.
Boil 3 cups water with a pinch of rock salt. Reduce to medium flame; add ground rice and almond powders, stirring continuously to prevent lumps.
Cook ~5 min until done. Add ghee and rock sugar; mix well. Serve.

sources.text: Morningstar — Ayurvedic Cooking for All, 3rd repr. 2011

description: Rice Pudding is an Ayurvedic rice preparation made with rice, dates and cinnamon powder, cooked all ingredients together with the appropriate q… — a classical recipe from Gowans. Cow's milk (Dugdha) builds Ojas — the body's vital essence.

steps.text: Cook all ingredients together with the appropriate quantity of water in a vessel or cooker.
Add more milk/water for a creamier texture.
Serve warm.

sources.text: Gowans — Food for Life: Ayurvedic Recipes, 2009

description: Rice & Date Pudding is an Ayurvedic rice preparation made with cooked rice, milk and dates, chopped, boiled milk — a classical recipe from Gowans. Cow's milk (Dugdha) builds Ojas — the body's vital essence.

steps.text: Boil milk; add chopped dates and stir until milk turns a brown colour.
Add cooked rice; simmer until mixture thickens (add more milk if needed).
Once creamy, switch off flame. Serve.

sources.text: Gowans — Food for Life: Ayurvedic Recipes, 2009
